newsitem.title: INDIA: Japan offers India biggest bilateral aid package.
newsitem.headline: Japan offers India biggest bilateral aid package.

text.p: Japan agreed on Monday to offer 133.7 billion yen ($1.15 billion) in concessional loans and grants to India, the largest bilateral aid package for New Delhi, the Japanese embassy said.
Among the 11 projects selected for assistance, seven were for infrastructure development, including five in the power sector and two in transport, the embassy said in a release.
"Japan maintains the position of being the largest bilateral donor of bilateral assistance to India, a position it has been holding since 1986, except in 1990," it said.
The package included 132.7 billion yen ($1.14 billion) in soft loans carrying interest rates of 2.3 percent with 30-year maturities, including a grace period of 10 years.
The assistance covered India's 1996/97 fiscal year ending on March 31.
The loan amount represented an increase of 3.1 percent over the previous fiscal year, the statement said.

The largest loan, for 19.82 billion yen ($170 million), will support the construction of a 1,000-megawatt coal-fired thermal power station in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh by the National Thermal Power Corp Ltd.

A 15.97 billion yen ($137 million) loan will help to preserve forests in the southern state of Karnataka, while a 14.76 billion yen ($127 million) loan will help to pay for a new commuter railway transport system in Delhi.
